title: Additive quasi-coherent quotient of consecutive nilpotent-units kernels
statement: Let $X$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $E_j$ denote the kernel sheaves of [def-sc-reduction-units-power-kernel]. For each $j\geq0$ there exist a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $F_j$ and a short exact complex of abelian etale sheaves $0\to E_{j+1}\to E_j\to (F_j)_{\mathrm{Et}}\to0$ [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module]. The associated additive sheaf is lifted sectionwise to the coefficient universe of $\mathbf G_m$. No Noetherian or finite nilpotence assumption is required.

source.place: Proof, Step 1 and the following Claim; proof text retained in the parent DAG node

proof.text: Put F_j=N^(j+1)/N^(j+2). Powers of a quasi-coherent ideal and their quotient are quasi-coherent. On each affine etale object, the base change of V(N^(j+1)) is the quotient by the extended ideal power; therefore E_j consists of units 1+a with a in that extended power.

The map 1+a to the class of a in F_j is compatible with restrictions, by etale flatness and its preservation of ideal quotients. It is a group homomorphism because the cross term ab lies in N^(2j+2), hence in N^(j+2). Its kernel is E_(j+1). On each etale affine object a quotient class lifts to a; every element of the extended nilradical is nilpotent, so 1+a is a unit. This proves local surjectivity and hence the short exact sequence. Sectionwise universe lift preserves exactness. The case j=0 uses 2=2; the zero ideal and empty scheme give zero sheaves.
